one_line: Browser agents create inspectable, wallet-free token swap plans.
what_it_does: Resolves assets, obtains fresh quotes, and returns unsigned swap plans with route, bounds, fees, warnings, expiry, and network context.
leverage_rationale: Typed public tools materially improve precision and freshness for asset resolution and quote planning, while the shared UI exposes the same plan; general UI-driving agents would be less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description specify nine public WebMCP tools for status, asset search, quotes, plans, and pools.
Frame sheet shows structured swap definition, quote, diagnostics/provenance, and agent-results areas.
Plans are explicitly unsigned and cannot execute or sign transactions.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, bounded planning workflow and a live demo link, with visible structured quote and provenance states; no submitted video and limited legible end-to-end evidence prevent a higher score.
execution_evidence: demo_alive is alive and public repository is reported.
Frame sheet visibly shows define-swap and agent-results UI with a quoted amount and diagnostics.
Devpost packaging screenshot shows the claimed product interface but is not runtime proof.
impact_rationale: Crypto users and browser agents have a concrete need for accurate route, fee, slippage, and freshness information before wallet actions; the wallet-free boundary is useful and credible.
impact_evidence: Description identifies asset discovery, precise amounts, route comparison, fees, price impact, and freshness as the problem.
Workflow returns warnings and unsigned metadata without unattended trading.
creativity_rationale: The wallet-free, agent-native swap-planning boundary and inspectable diagnostics are a fresh application of WebMCP, though swap quoting itself is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Agent plans rather than signs or submits transactions.
Shared planning workflow and provenance are emphasized.
usability_note: Structured plan, warnings, expiry, and explicit wallet boundary suggest good diagnostic usability; actual interaction is not fully observable.
red_flags: No submitted video despite referenced frame sheets; frame text is low resolution.
No wallet access or executable transaction is demonstrated.
standouts: Clear safety boundary: unsigned, canExecute false, requiresWallet false.
Fresh quote and provenance make WebMCP consequential rather than cosmetic.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP fit and credible finance utility, with a coherent demonstrated planning surface despite thin video evidence.

one_line: Agent-native automotive configurator, garage digital twin, guide, and 3D creation engine.
what_it_does: Lets agents and people inspect and revise a shared fictional vehicle build, calculate ownership outcomes, manipulate a 3D vehicle, and inspect components and modeling workflow.
leverage_rationale: A shared, revision-gated 3D vehicle state with 49 typed tools, attribution, undo, component measurement, and human interruption is substantially beyond reliable generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Description states five contexts and 49 WebMCP registrations.
Human and agent mutations use shared state, are revision-gated and undoable, and identify source or measurement basis.
Frame sheet shows automotive landing/configuration surfaces, though detailed tool calls are not legible.
execution_rationale: The submission describes an unusually broad but coherent suite and has a live demo and public repo; visual evidence is mostly splash/landing states and does not clearly prove the central workflow end to end.
execution_evidence: demo_alive is alive; public repository reported.
Frame sheet visibly shows AutoLab branding, agent-native positioning, three experiences, and a creation-engine surface.
Build stack and test technologies are explicitly listed.
impact_rationale: Car enthusiasts, configurators, and owners have a clear desire for understandable, inspectable vehicle exploration and co-creation; value is credible but the fictional vehicle limits immediate practical scope.
impact_evidence: Description targets car lovers and shared vehicle journey.
Tools cover pricing, ownership outcomes, component inspection, and configuration.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-native configurator, synchronized garage digital twin, visual owner's guide, and measurement-driven 3D creation engine is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Four integrated automotive experiences share one vehicle.
42 named components and measurement-driven reconstruction are claimed.
usability_note: Undo, interruption, shared state, and source-basis labeling are strong usability choices, but the packet does not show enough readable task flow.
red_flags: Very broad scope with limited legible runtime evidence.
Vehicle is a fictional independent reconstruction, not manufacturer CAD.
standouts: Agent/human shared reducer and revision-gated mutations.
Deep component-level 3D inspection rather than a chat wrapper.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity; execution evidence is incomplete but the concept and architecture are strong.

one_line: Agent-assisted video clipping workspace for finding and precisely editing shareable moments.
what_it_does: Helps locate moments in uploaded videos, make precise cuts, and collaborate with a human editor on social-ready clips.
leverage_rationale: Structured editing tools can reduce tedious, precision-sensitive UI work and support shared human-agent editing, but a general-purpose agent could plausibly achieve much of the same outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly frames WebMCP as assisting moment finding and cuts while the human edits by hand.
Frame sheet shows a Make a Moment media workspace with a populated preview and instruction-like side panel.
Agent results are not clearly legible.
execution_rationale: A populated media preview and coherent editing surface suggest a plausible product, but the packet lacks a public repo and video evidence is repetitive and low resolution.
execution_evidence: demo_alive is alive and five gallery images are reported.
Frame sheet shows a dark media workflow with preview and controls.
No video transcript or submitted video is present.
impact_rationale: Creators and gaming communities have a concrete, recurring need to find and prepare clips; the founder cites prior use by a large Tekken community and a specific tedious workflow.
impact_evidence: Description identifies precision timing and mental/tedius clipping work.
Prior tool reportedly served over 30,000 Tekken players.
Cloud storage and sharing are part of the workflow.
creativity_rationale: Human-in-the-goop co-editing for video clipping is a fresh synthesis with a clear agent role, though clipping is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Agent helps with moment selection and cuts while retaining hand editing.
Revival of a real community clipping workflow gives the concept specificity.
usability_note: Human editing alongside agent assistance is a sensible model; detailed controls and completion states are not legible.

Frame evidence is repetitive and does not clearly show tool calls or export completion.
standouts: Specific creator pain point with credible prior audience.
Human-agent co-editing rather than full automation.
advance_reason: Strong audience/problem fit and meaningful agent-assisted editing, though runtime proof is thin.

one_line: WebMCP claims-intake agent that explains coverage and prepares a first notice of loss.
what_it_does: Reads insurer rules as typed tools, drafts a claim from plain-language crash details, identifies required fields, and refuses unsafe or unauthorized changes before human filing.
leverage_rationale: Policy-specific typed tools, live tool-surface changes, clause-linked requirements, refusal of prompt injection, and human-only filing make structured page tools central and hard to replicate reliably with generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Description says agent discovers insurer typed tools at runtime and drafts claims from plain words.
Tool availability changes with answers; a planted third-party instruction is refused with PATCH_REJECTED_LOCKED.
Claim is not filed and File this claim remains a human action.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a detailed, safety-conscious central workflow and frame sheet visibly shows structured claim, missing-intake, and follow-up panels; exact tool traces are not legible and no video is submitted.
execution_evidence: demo_alive is alive; public MIT repository reported.
Frame sheet visibly shows a claim workspace with what intake still needs and to-call-later outputs.
Description names dynamic tool publication, ledger refusal, and unfiled human handoff.
impact_rationale: Drivers in a crash have an urgent, specific information problem, while insurers need complete first notices; policy-specific coverage explanation and follow-up reduction directly address it.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets FNOL and explains coverage while reporting a crash.
Workflow identifies missing requirements and creates a focused follow-up list.
Human filing boundary preserves control in a consequential domain.
creativity_rationale: The combination of live typed policy surfaces, clause-level provenance, adversarial instruction refusal, and human-only filing is an original and memorable insurance interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Dynamic ninth tool appears when the driver says the car cannot be driven and withdraws when changed back.
PATCH_REJECTED_LOCKED ledger behavior is explicitly demonstrated.
usability_note: The structured intake, clause-linked requirements, refusal ledger, and explicit human handoff are unusually clear safety/usability choices.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame-sheet text is only partly legible.
Coverage and claim behavior are demonstrated as a prototype, not a production insurer integration.
standouts: Strong safety boundary and prompt-injection resistance.
WebMCP tool surface adapts to state and exposes policy-specific rules.
advance_reason: Best-in-packet combination of indispensable WebMCP leverage, concrete urgent impact, and credible safety-aware execution.

one_line: Supervised studio where agents author fictional coding sessions rendered to SVG and video.
what_it_does: Lets an agent write and direct scripts, control surfaces and cameras, preview timing and frames, propose human-approved rewrites, and export deterministic media.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on live stage state with inspectable timing/frame tools, approval-gated patches, undo, and export; generic UI driving would be less precise and less reproducible.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly describes load_script, direct_camera, inspect_timeline, snapshot_frame, fit_duration, propose_patch, approve_proposal, and export.
Agent rail logs calls and every word on stage is listed.
Export is approval-gated and deterministic SVG/CSS is produced.
execution_rationale: The 170-second video transcript describes a complete workflow from script authoring through choices, voice input, restyling, terminal surface, and approved export; frame sheets show studio/browser integration.
execution_evidence: Submitted 170-second video with detailed transcript.
Transcript covers script load, playback, choice interaction, voice input, style change, terminal surface, and export.
Frame sheet visibly shows staged agent studio and tool-registration context.
impact_rationale: Developers, educators, documentation authors, and presenters have a real need for privacy-safe, repeatable agent-session media that can be edited and re-shot without leaking secrets.
impact_evidence: About text names READMEs, docs, talks, and posts as use cases.
Client-only rendering and deterministic export address privacy and re-shootability.
creativity_rationale: Treating a fictional coding-agent session as a directed stage with timing, choices, voice, camera, and deterministic SVG/video output is a distinctive interaction model pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Agent acts on the stage itself and can inspect exact frame/timeline facts.
Choice beats, voice input, styling, and two surfaces demonstrate breadth within one concept.
usability_note: Approval cards, undo, call rail, privacy default, and full-text stage inventory support reviewability and control.

standouts: Rarely complete evidence of tool calls, live result changes, review controls, and export.

advance_reason: Complete demonstrated workflow, strong WebMCP delta, and highly original creative product with clear audience value.
